newsitem.title: CANADA: No progress at Canadian Air talks - unions.
newsitem.headline: No progress at Canadian Air talks - unions.

text.p: Talks aimed at convincing two holdout unions to support a rescue plan for troubled Canadian Airlines Corp made little progress early Friday, officials said.

Canadian Auto Workers union President Buzz Hargrove met Canadian Transport Minister David Anderson but said the late-night discussions produced no progress. It was a "disappointing" session that amounted to "another lecture that the company is in trouble," he told reporters.
He described Ottawa's aid offer for the struggling airline as "an insult."

Canadian Union of Public Employees president Judy Darcy also reported no progress after a meeting with Anderson and promised further talks through the night with her union delegation. "We're not happy with their (Ottawa's) answer, but we're not giving up either," she said.
